denial.text: Saltmarsh Benefits Administrators denied the claim for CPT 19357 (breast reconstruction with tissue expander) with date of service 2026-07-28. CARC 197: Precertification/authorization/notification/pre-treatment absent. Payer remark: No authorization is on file. A retrospective medical necessity review may be requested with supporting clinical documentation within 180 days.

criteria.text: Documented mastectomy for breast cancer, or prophylactic mastectomy for a qualifying risk, with reconstruction requested by the patient. Reconstruction after a covered mastectomy is a mandated benefit under the Women’s Health and Cancer Rights Act.
An operative plan for staged reconstruction (tissue expander placement followed by implant exchange) appropriate to the patient’s radiation status and tissue quality.
Medical clearance for the planned surgery is documented.

chart.text: A1c came back 6.5. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 5 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.

Here with a cough and congestion for 4 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

From the breast surgeon: right total mastectomy performed 7 months ago for a 1.7 centimeter invasive ductal carcinoma, sentinel nodes negative, margins clear. She has completed adjuvant chemotherapy and wishes to proceed with reconstruction.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

56 year old woman referred by the breast surgeon for reconstruction. Went over expanders versus flaps, she prefers the expander route, fewer operations and no donor site. Her history otherwise: migraines, rare now, hypertension on lisinopril, mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year. Allergies: no drug allergies. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works retail. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Status post right mastectomy 7 months ago for a 1.7 centimeter invasive ductal. Done with chemo. She wants reconstruction and has thought hard about it. No radiation planned per oncology. Good skin envelope, no infection, mastectomy flap healed. Plan is a right tissue expander under the pectoralis now, exchange to a permanent implant in about 3 months, and a left lift for symmetry later.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 208, LDL 107, HDL 56, triglycerides 179. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Back with her sister to go over the plan again. Questions answered. Ready to schedule. Vitals today 131 over 84, pulse 75.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the scheduler.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Blood pressure check. 145 over 76 today, 127 over 93 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Pre-op. Cleared by her PCP, letter in the chart, labs and EKG fine. Consent signed for right tissue expander placement.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 197 denial can be answered from the record.
